description: Hand-written: the traversal.* kernel rows’ own contract (PL.native-traversal-rows slice 1, U106(1); core’s P9e kernels, P9e.core) — each row’s answer shape over core’s functions, the IR readers feeding the decision rows (the answer one row gives is what the next row is sent), core’s refusals as VALUES, the rows’ own refusals as errors coded [invalid-input], and the rows no corpus pins (the IR readers, a stated stamina on the route row, the ground-seat params on a settle). Every expectation here was computed by core’s own functions at the pin, not by these rows. Core’s own corpora (conformance/traversal/{affordances,vehicles,fast-travel,ground-seating}.json, 67 cases) are driven whole through these rows by the traversal_corpus ctest (tests/traversal_corpus.cpp), not transcribed here.

cases.name: traversal.affordances: a world IR block read into core’s tuning and links, then resolved, the best way and the route
traversal.affordances.route: stamina, when sent, reaches every leg the search resolves, as core’s findRoute reads it
traversal.affordances: the rows’ own refusals are errors coded [invalid-input]
traversal.vehicles: the IR’s vehicles read by core, boarded and driven, each answer core’s
traversal.vehicles: the rows’ own refusals are errors coded [invalid-input]
traversal.fastTravel: the IR’s tuning read by core, the ceiling, the hours and a plan priced from a route the route row answered
traversal.fastTravel: the rows’ own refusals are errors coded [invalid-input]
traversal.groundSeating: each row is core’s ground-seat function, the pack’s params read on every call, the settle over the state the last answer carried
traversal.groundSeating: the rows’ own refusals are errors coded [invalid-input]
